alignments.note: The ASV's recasting spends no English word on this `לְ`'s own relation; the object noun keeps its own *a man*, so rule 40 leaves the preposition unrepresented.

Wholly supplied lexical verb for a verbless clause; rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, corroborated by the ASV italics under rule 7. *hurt* predicates an event the Hebrew never wrote, so it is not rule 49's copular or result frame.
Noun with its own indefinite article under rule 15.
Comparative preposition is the predicate of the recast clause *as thou art*, so it carries the construction-supplied copula under rule 49; discontinuous around the suffix's *thou* under rule 25.
Second `לְ`, unrepresented on the same terms as the first.
Second wholly supplied lexical verb; same reasoning as *may hurt*.
Construct noun with its own indefinite article under rule 15.
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the noun.

review_notes: The materially different alternative gives *may hurt* and *may profit* to the two `לְ`s as rule 49 result frames. It is not taken because those verbs introduce an event and an affected object the Hebrew does not predicate, which is the boundary rule 20 draws against a supplied lexical verb; the ASV's italics corroborate without deciding, by rule 7.
